summary: Each lane's definition_paths in .st/required-lanes.json are now what defines its verdict: the files its commands execute, derived by scripts/lane-definition-closure, plus the data that sets its bar (baselines, splits, filters, the license inventory) declared in that script's VERDICT_DATA, instead of all of scripts/ and .st/. A change to a CI script is a lane edit (signed only in CI) only for the lanes that run it, and a workflow or doc a test only checks is the tree under test. scripts/lane-definition-closure-test and a whole-tree --check in genie-freshness hold every lane's executed files and verdict data inside its definition_paths

replay.detail: No record, signature or storage format changes.

schema.detail: No schema change; the lane file keeps its keys and shape.

rules.detail: Which tree edits count as lane edits changes per lane. linux-gate and rust-tests now list the test, clippy and fleet-compat stage scripts they run, the cargo and nextest configuration, and their verdict data (the daily-only filterset and the messaging compat baseline; linux-gate also the clippy baseline and splits and the fleet compat baseline). fractal-web lists its web scripts and runners, the web shell and its input spec, the Buck and pnpm files and the license inventory. typescript-client lists the package manifests whose scripts it runs and the web shell. ci-script-tests and genie-freshness keep scripts/, .st/ and the flake, and add only the files outside them that the walk finds they execute (the root pnpm files; for genie-freshness also the Buck, cargo and nextest configuration and the package manifests), not the docs or workflows their tests read.

compatibility.detail: Every lane's lane_definition_sha256 changes, so notes signed before this merges are wrong_definition against a base that has it, and pull requests opened earlier are held to the new definition (their branch point's lane file differs): sign such a head again with scripts/st-test, or CI runs the check.

manual.detail: None. After a change that makes a lane execute a new file, run scripts/lane-definition-closure --write and review the diff; a new file that sets a lane's bar goes in VERDICT_DATA with its reason.

recovery.detail: Revert .st/required-lanes.json to the wide lists; the lane file is read from the base, so it takes effect for runs after the revert merges.
